prompt:
Our run book has a step where somebody opens VMware Cloud Foundation Operations and pastes the same triage note onto every critical alert. We want that unattended, and we want it to survive the session going stale, because on a busy appliance it does: `acquireToken` hands back a token with a stated `validity`, and the appliance can still decide it is finished before then. When that happens the next call answers `401` in the middle of a batch that is already half done.

This repo has the skeleton. `docs/contract.json` is the wire contract, derived from the VCF Operations OpenAPI specification at tag 9.0.0.0, and `docs/official_sources.json` records where it came from. Both are pinned inputs — read them, don't edit them.

Implement the `vcfops_triage` package under `src/vcfops_triage/` so that `python -m vcfops_triage` annotates the matching alerts end to end and writes its report to `--output`. `README.md` has the full argument list, the report shape and the exit codes we need.

The part to be careful about: recovering from that `401` without losing or repeating work. Walk the alert pages in order and annotate a page before you fetch the next one. When a call comes back `401`, acquire a new token and re-send **that one request** with it — don't start the batch over, don't re-fetch a page you already have, and don't add a second note to an alert the server already accepted one for. Bound the number of re-acquisitions with `--max-refreshes`; when that budget is gone and the token is still rejected, exit `5` without trying to release anything.

Be strict about optional inputs. With no `--auth-source`, that key must not appear in the `acquireToken` body at all — not `null`, not `""`. With no `--alert-name`, the `alert-query` body carries no `alertName` key; an omitted criterion means "do not filter on this", so there is no empty version of it. With no `--page-size`, `pageSize` is not on the URL at all and the server's documented default applies. And the note body carries `content` and nothing else — the alert id goes in the path. Validate `--criticality` and `--page-size` against the contract before opening a connection, so we never put a request the 9.0 contract forbids on the wire.

Standard library only, no third-party packages.

`tools/mock_ops_server.py` is a loopback mock of the four operations the contract names; it enforces the contract, retires tokens on a request count rather than a clock, and logs every request it receives, so you can run the flow by hand and see exactly what you sent. `./run_verification.sh` is the acceptance test and must pass.
